examples.ko: 밀알 한 알이 땅에 떨어져 싹이 텄어요.
examples.en: A single grain of wheat fell to the ground and sprouted.

examples.ko: 농부가 밭에 밀알을 정성껏 뿌렸어요.
examples.en: The farmer carefully sowed wheat grains in the field.

examples.ko: 새들이 밀알을 쪼아 먹고 있어요.
examples.en: Birds are pecking at the wheat grains.

examples.ko: 이 빵은 밀알이 그대로 씹혀서 고소해요.
examples.en: You can chew the whole wheat grains in this bread, so it tastes nutty.

examples.ko: 작은 밀알도 모이면 큰 힘이 돼요.
examples.en: Even small grains of wheat become a great force when they gather.

examples.ko: 밀알처럼 작은 도움이 세상을 바꿀 수 있어요.
examples.en: Small help, like a grain of wheat, can change the world.

explain: 밀의 낟알 하나하나를 말해요. 작지만 싹이 터서 열매를 맺는 모습 때문에 비유로도 쓰여요. '쌀알'처럼 '-알'이 붙은 말과 같은 방식이에요.

phrases.en: I also want to be a grain of wheat for society.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 위해 작지만 소중한 힘을 보태는 사람이 된다는 뜻으로, 다짐이나 연설에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means becoming someone who contributes a small but precious effort for others, and is used in resolutions or speeches.

explain_en: Wheat kernel; also a symbol of sacrifice. It refers to each individual kernel of wheat. Because a small kernel can sprout and bear fruit, it is also used figuratively. It is formed like '쌀알', with '-알' attached.

en: table side; at the dinner table (mealtime)

examples.ko: 밥상머리 교육은 가정에서 시작돼요.
examples.en: Table manners education starts at home.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 밥상머리에서 휴대폰을 안 봐요.
examples.en: In our house, we don't look at phones at the dinner table.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 밥상머리에서 늘 예절을 가르치셨어요.
examples.en: Grandfather always taught us manners at the dinner table.

examples.ko: 밥상머리에서 그런 얘기는 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't talk about that kind of thing at the table.

examples.ko: 밥상머리 대화가 아이에게 큰 도움이 된대요.
examples.en: They say conversation at the dinner table helps children a lot.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 밥상머리에서 들은 말이 아직도 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember what I heard at the dinner table as a child.

explain: '밥상머리 교육'처럼 식사 자리에서 어른에게 배우는 예절과 대화를 말할 때 많이 써요. 밥상 위의 음식이 아니라 밥 먹는 자리 그 곁을 가리켜요. 그냥 식탁을 말할 때는 '식탁'이나 '밥상'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Table manners are learned in childhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식사 자리에서 지켜야 하는 예의를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the manners one should keep at mealtime.

phrases.example: 밥상머리 대화가 가족을 가깝게 해 줘요.
phrases.en: Conversations at the dinner table bring a family closer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이 밥 먹으며 나누는 이야기를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to talk that a family has while eating.

phrases.en: Please don't look at your phone at the dining table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가구로서의 식사용 탁자를 말할 때는 '식탁'이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: When you mean the table as furniture, 식탁 is more natural.

explain_en: It is often used in '밥상머리 교육', meaning the manners and talk children learn from elders at mealtime. It points to the place beside the table where people eat, not the food on it. For the table itself, people just say '식탁' or '밥상'.

t90.ax: Table manners education starts at home.

examples.ko: 아이 입가에 밥풀이 하나 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There is a grain of rice stuck at the corner of the child's mouth.

examples.ko: 손에 붙은 밥풀을 떼어 내기가 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to get the rice stuck on my hand off.

examples.ko: 밥풀 몇 개로 봉투를 붙였어요.
examples.en: I sealed the envelope with a few grains of rice.

examples.ko: 설거지할 때 그릇에 말라붙은 밥풀은 물에 불려요.
examples.en: When I wash dishes, I soak the dried-on rice grains in water.

examples.ko: 옷에 밥풀 묻은 줄도 모르고 하루 종일 다녔어요.
examples.en: I went around all day without noticing there was rice on my clothes.

examples.ko: 김밥을 싸다 보니 손이 밥풀투성이가 됐어요.
examples.en: While rolling gimbap, my hands ended up covered in rice.

explain: '밥알'과 거의 비슷하지만, 입가나 손, 옷에 붙어 있는 밥 한 톨을 말할 때 특히 잘 써요. '입가에 밥풀이 묻었어요'처럼 '붙다·묻다'와 자주 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: There is a grain of rice stuck on your cheek.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥풀이 어딘가에 달라붙어 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a grain of rice sticking to something.

phrases.en: There is a grain of rice on my clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '붙다'보다 살짝 묻은 느낌이 있어서 옷이나 입가에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '묻다' feels lighter than '붙다' and is often used for clothes or around the mouth.
phrases.en_equiv: a grain of rice gets on

phrases.en: I pick the grain of rice off my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙어 있는 밥풀을 직접 떼어 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you remove a grain of rice that is stuck on.
phrases.en_equiv: to pick off a grain of rice

explain_en: Sticky rice bits on clothes, face, bowl, spoken. It is close to '밥알', but it is especially natural for rice stuck to the mouth, hands or clothes. It often goes with verbs like '붙다' and '묻다', as in '입가에 밥풀이 묻었어요'.

t90.ax: I sealed the envelope with a few grains of rice.

examples.ko: 바닷물은 염분이 높아서 짜요.
examples.en: Sea water is salty because its salt content is high.

examples.ko: 의사가 염분을 줄이라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to reduce my salt intake.

examples.ko: 라면 국물에는 염분이 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Ramen broth has a lot of salt in it.

examples.ko: 염분이 많은 땅에서는 농사가 어려워요.
examples.en: Farming is hard on land with a lot of salt.

examples.ko: 땀을 흘리면 염분도 같이 빠져나가요.
examples.en: When you sweat, salt leaves your body too.

examples.ko: 이 간장은 염분이 적어서 건강에 좋아요.
examples.en: This soy sauce is low in salt, so it's healthy.

explain: '소금'은 우리가 직접 뿌려 먹는 재료이고, '염분'은 음식이나 바닷물에 들어 있는 소금 성분이에요. 건강 이야기에서는 '염분을 줄이다', '염분을 섭취하다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '나트륨'은 영양 표시에 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I'm trying to eat food that is low in salt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에 소금 성분이 적을 때 써요. 반대는 '염분이 높다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when food has little salt. The opposite is 염분이 높다.

phrases.example: 염분을 너무 많이 섭취하면 몸에 안 좋아요.
phrases.en: Taking in too much salt is bad for your body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강 이야기에서 소금 성분을 먹는다는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say taking in salt, used in health talk.

phrases.en: This snack has a lot of sodium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영양 표시에 쓰는 말이에요. '염분'은 소금 성분 전체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word used on nutrition labels, while 염분 refers to salt content in general.

explain_en: 소금 is the ingredient you sprinkle, while 염분 is the salt component inside food or sea water. In health talk you say 염분을 줄이다 or 염분을 섭취하다. 나트륨 is the term you see on nutrition labels.

en: to grab a bite; to appease one's hunger

examples.ko: 배고플 때 빵으로 간단히 요기했어요.
examples.en: When I was hungry, I had a quick bite with some bread.

examples.ko: 점심 전에 김밥으로 요기하고 갈게요.
examples.en: I'll have some gimbap to tide me over and then go.

examples.ko: 요기할 만한 게 없어서 편의점에 들렀어요.
examples.en: There was nothing to snack on, so I stopped by a convenience store.

examples.ko: 손님이 오기 전에 떡으로 요기해 두세요.
examples.en: Have some rice cake to tide you over before the guests arrive.

examples.ko: 오래 걸릴 테니 먼저 요기부터 하세요.
examples.en: It will take a while, so grab a bite first.

examples.ko: 요기하는 정도라서 많이 안 먹었어요.
examples.en: It was just to tide me over, so I didn't eat much.

explain: 배가 너무 고프지 않게 조금만 먹을 때 써요. '식사하다'는 한 끼를 제대로 먹는 것이고, 요기하다는 간단히 때우는 쪽이에요. '요기를 하다'처럼 '요기'만 써도 돼요. '여기'의 말투인 '요기'와는 다른 낱말이에요.

phrases.en: I was late, so I grabbed a bite at a convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요기'만 명사로 써서 간단히 먹는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 'yogi' as a noun for eating a little.

phrases.en: Have a quick bite before you go.
phrases.nuance_ko: '간단히'를 붙이면 조금만 먹는다는 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'simply' makes it clearer you'll eat only a little.

phrases.en: Even one piece of bread is enough to tide you over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 먹어서 배고픔이 잠깐 가라앉았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a small bite eases your hunger for a while.

explain_en: Use it when you eat just a little so you aren't too hungry. 식사하다 is eating a proper meal, while 요기하다 is getting by with something small. You can also say 요기를 하다. It is a different word from the 요기 that means 여기.

examples.ko: 영화 볼 때 주전부리를 사 갈까요?
examples.en: Shall we buy some snacks to bring when we watch the movie?

examples.ko: 할머니 댁에 가면 주전부리가 항상 많아요.
examples.en: There are always lots of snacks at Grandma's house.

examples.ko: 주전부리로 과일이나 견과류를 먹어요.
examples.en: I eat fruit or nuts as snacks.

examples.ko: 밤에 주전부리 때문에 자꾸 살이 쪄요.
examples.en: I keep gaining weight because of late-night snacking.

examples.ko: 주전부리는 끊기가 정말 어려워요.
examples.en: Snacking is really hard to quit.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 주전부리도 꼭 챙겨요.
examples.en: When I travel, I always pack snacks too.

explain: 끼니 사이에 입이 심심해서 이것저것 먹는 과자, 과일 같은 간식을 말해요. '간식'보다 가볍고 친근한 느낌이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '군것질'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: If I snack a lot, I lose my appetite for meals.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주전부리'와 거의 같은 뜻으로, 먹는 행동을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 주전부리, but used more for the act of snacking.

phrases.en: If you snack at night, you gain weight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간식을 먹는 행동을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for the act of eating snacks.

phrases.en: I bought some snacks at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과자나 간식거리를 살 때 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light way to say you bought snacks.

explain_en: It refers to the snacks, such as crackers or fruit, that you nibble on between meals when your mouth feels bored. It sounds lighter and more casual than '간식'. '군것질' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

t90.ax: I eat fruit or nuts as snacks.

examples.ko: 이 과자에는 첨가물이 거의 안 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This snack has almost no additives in it.

examples.ko: 식품 첨가물은 포장지 뒤에 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: Food additives are listed on the back of the package.

examples.ko: 첨가물이 없는 주스를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought juice with no additives.

examples.ko: 아이에게 첨가물 많은 음식을 주고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to give my child food full of additives.

examples.ko: 화학 첨가물을 줄이는 회사가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More companies are cutting back on chemical additives.

examples.ko: 첨가물 때문에 맛이 좀 이상해졌어요.
examples.en: The taste turned a bit strange because of the additives.

explain: '재료'는 음식의 기본이 되는 것이고, '첨가물'은 맛이나 색, 보관을 위해 따로 더한 것이에요. 포장지에서 '식품 첨가물', '무첨가'라는 말을 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: I'm worried about food additives, so I read the ingredient list.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말로, 포장지와 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, seen on packages and in the news.

phrases.en: This juice has no added sugar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 첨가물을 넣지 않았다는 뜻으로 포장지에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Printed on packaging to mean nothing was added.

phrases.example: 이 음식에는 색소 첨가물이 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: This food contains coloring additives.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어 있는 상태를 말할 때 '들어 있다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '들어 있다' to say something is contained.

explain_en: 재료 is what a dish is basically made of, while 첨가물 is something added separately for taste, color or storage. You often see 식품 첨가물 and 무첨가 on packaging.

en: to go broke; to go bankrupt

examples.ko: 사업이 잘못되는 바람에 집안이 거덜나서 이사했어요.
examples.en: The business failed and the family went broke, so we moved.

examples.ko: 씀씀이가 크면 재산이 금방 거덜나요.
examples.en: If you spend freely, your fortune runs out quickly.

examples.ko: 이번 달 월급이 벌써 거덜났어요.
examples.en: This month's pay is already gone.

examples.ko: 큰 병이 나면 살림이 거덜나곤 해요.
examples.en: When someone gets seriously ill, a household often goes broke.

examples.ko: 그 가게 때문에 가족 재산이 거덜날 뻔했어요.
examples.en: Because of that shop, the family's wealth almost vanished.

examples.ko: 이러다 통장이 거덜나겠어요.
examples.en: At this rate, my bank account will be wiped out.

explain: 재산, 돈, 살림, 가게 같은 것이 거의 다 없어질 때 써요. '망하다'는 사업이나 사람이 주어가 되는 일이 많고, 거덜나다는 돈과 살림이 바닥나는 데 초점이 있어요. 남이 그렇게 만들 때는 '거덜을 내다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Because of gambling, the household went broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살림'과 함께 쓰면 가정의 돈이 바닥나는 느낌이 잘 살아요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'household,' it clearly conveys the family's money running out.

phrases.en: He failed at investing and wiped out his fortune.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 달리 누가 그렇게 만들었는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike the headword, it says who caused the ruin.

phrases.en: Spend carefully so your money doesn't run out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않게'와 함께 쓰면 조심하라는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-지 않게,' it becomes a warning to be careful.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to go broke

explain_en: It is used when assets, money, a household or a shop is almost entirely gone. '망하다' often takes a business or person as the subject, while 거덜나다 focuses on money and livelihood running dry. When someone causes it, people say '거덜을 내다'.

en: to be frugal; to be thrifty

examples.ko: 할머니는 평생 검약하게 사셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother lived frugally all her life.

examples.ko: 검약한 생활 덕분에 집을 살 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a thrifty lifestyle, I was able to buy a house.

examples.ko: 부모님은 검약해서 필요 없는 물건을 사지 않으세요.
examples.en: My parents are thrifty and don't buy things they don't need.

examples.ko: 그분은 부자지만 아주 검약하는 편이에요.
examples.en: He is rich but tends to be very frugal.

examples.ko: 월급이 줄어서 올해는 더 검약해야 해요.
examples.en: My salary went down, so I have to be even more frugal this year.

examples.ko: 검약하고 부지런한 사람이 되라고 아버지가 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: My father told me to become a thrifty and hardworking person.

explain: '절약하다'는 돈이나 물건을 아껴 쓰는 행동에 두루 쓰고, '검약하다'는 사치하지 않고 소박하게 사는 태도에 더 가까워서 글이나 어른들 말씀에서 많이 보여요. '근검절약'이라는 짝말도 함께 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: My parents lived a frugal life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form used to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: Even with lots of money, he lives frugally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사는 방식을 말할 때 '-게'로 바꿔서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Change it to -게 to describe a way of living.

phrases.en: Being thrifty is our family's way of life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부지런하고 아껴 쓴다는 뜻의 짝말이에요. 글이나 훈계하는 말에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: This phrase means working hard and spending carefully, often seen in writing or advice.

explain_en: '절약하다' covers the act of saving money or things in general, while '검약하다' is closer to a modest, non-extravagant way of living and shows up more in writing or elders' speech. Also remember the set phrase '근검절약'.

t90.ax: He is rich but tends to be very frugal.

examples.ko: 요즘 돈에 궁해서 외식을 못 해요.
examples.en: I'm short of money these days, so I can't eat out.

examples.ko: 궁할 때 도와준 친구를 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't forget the friend who helped me when I was in need.

examples.ko: 그는 살림이 궁해도 늘 웃어요.
examples.en: He always smiles even when money is tight.

examples.ko: 궁한 처지에 놓인 이웃을 도왔어요.
examples.en: I helped a neighbor who was in a difficult situation.

examples.ko: 돈이 궁하다고 해서 아무한테나 빌리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even if you're short of money, you shouldn't borrow from just anyone.

examples.ko: 갑자기 질문을 받으니 대답이 궁해요.
examples.en: I was asked suddenly, so I'm at a loss for an answer.

explain: '가난하다'와 달리 돈, 대답, 방법처럼 꼭 필요한 것이 모자라서 곤란한 상황에 초점이 있어요. '돈에 궁하다', '대답이 궁하다'처럼 '~에/이 궁하다' 꼴로 써요.

phrases.en: I helped a neighbor who was in need.
phrases.nuance_ko: '궁한 + 명사'로 어렵고 곤란한 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '궁한 + noun' describes a difficult, needy situation.

phrases.en: I was stuck for an answer because they asked suddenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 아니라 말이 모자라 곤란할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can also mean being at a loss for words, not only for money.
phrases.en_equiv: be at a loss for an answer

phrases.en: I'm not short of money right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 필요한 것이 모자라지 않다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says you are not lacking what you need.

explain_en: Unlike '가난하다' (poor), it focuses on being in a tight spot because something you need, like money, an answer or a way out, is lacking. It is used in patterns like '돈에 궁하다' and '대답이 궁하다'.

en: to be torn off; to be bitten; to be fleeced (of money)

examples.ko: 모기한테 다리를 많이 뜯겼어요.
examples.en: My legs got bitten a lot by mosquitoes.

examples.ko: 정비소에서 수리비를 너무 많이 뜯겼어요.
examples.en: I got ripped off with a really high repair bill at the garage.

examples.ko: 태풍에 간판이 뜯겨서 길에 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The signboard was torn off in the typhoon and fell on the street.

examples.ko: 강아지한테 신발이 다 뜯겼어요.
examples.en: My shoes got chewed up all over by the puppy.

examples.ko: 택배 상자가 이미 뜯겨 있었어요.
examples.en: The delivery box had already been torn open.

examples.ko: 벽지가 오래돼서 군데군데 뜯겨요.
examples.en: The wallpaper is old, so it's peeling off in places.

explain: '뜯다'의 피동으로, 붙은 것이 떨어져 나가거나 모기·동물에게 물어뜯길 때 써요. '돈을 뜯기다'처럼 바가지를 쓰거나 억지로 돈을 빼앗길 때도 써요. 하는 쪽에는 '한테/에게'를 붙여서 '모기한테 뜯기다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: My older brother squeezed my allowance out of me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 억지로 돈을 빼앗길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when money is taken from you by force or pressure.

phrases.en: I got bitten by mosquitoes a lot at the campsite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모기나 벌레에 물릴 때 '에게/한테'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '에게/한테' when bugs bite you.

phrases.en: The wind was strong, so the sign got torn off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙어 있던 것이 떨어져 나갔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something attached gets torn away.

explain_en: It is the passive of '뜯다', used when something is torn off or when you get bitten by mosquitoes or animals. It is also used for being overcharged or having money taken, as in '돈을 뜯기다'. The doer takes '한테/에게', as in '모기한테 뜯기다'.

en: to squander; to run through; to waste

examples.ko: 형이 사업에 실패해서 가진 돈을 다 털어먹었어요.
examples.en: My older brother failed in business and ran through all his money.

examples.ko: 월급을 한 달 만에 다 털어먹으면 어떡해요?
examples.en: What are you going to do if you blow your whole salary in one month?

examples.ko: 아버지가 물려주신 땅을 털어먹고 말았어요.
examples.en: He ended up squandering the land his father left him.

examples.ko: 용돈을 게임에 털어먹어서 이번 달은 빈털터리예요.
examples.en: I blew my allowance on games, so I am broke this month.

examples.ko: 퇴직금을 주식으로 털어먹었다는 소문이 돌아요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that he lost his whole severance pay on stocks.

examples.ko: 집안 재산을 털어먹은 삼촌 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard the story of my uncle who squandered the family fortune.

explain: 재산이나 돈을 헛되이 다 써 버렸다는 뜻으로 속된 느낌이 있어서, 격식 있는 자리에서는 '탕진하다'라고 해요. 목적어는 보통 재산, 돈, 월급처럼 돈과 관련된 말이에요. 사업이나 일을 망칠 때는 '말아먹다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: He gambled away all his fortune.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이나 재산을 목적어로 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, with money or property as the object.

phrases.example: 그는 유산을 몇 년 만에 탕진했어요.
phrases.en: He squandered his inheritance in a few years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 속된 느낌이 없어서 격식 있는 자리에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning without the slangy tone, so it suits formal settings.

phrases.en: My brother ruined his business and was left with only debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 아니라 사업이나 일을 망칠 때 쓰는 속된 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slangy word used for ruining a business or a job, not for spending money.

explain_en: Colloquial, blunt; blow all one's money, lose everything. It carries a slangy, informal feel of using up money or property in a wasteful way, so in formal settings people say '탕진하다'. Its objects are usually money-related, such as property, money or salary. When someone ruins a business or a job, '말아먹다' is also used.

t90.ax: He ended up squandering the land his father left him.

examples.ko: 요즘 아이 성적이 가장 큰 근심거리예요.
examples.en: These days my child's grades are my biggest worry.

examples.ko: 근심거리가 없으면 잠이 잘 올 텐데요.
examples.en: If I had no worries, I could sleep well.

examples.ko: 부모님께는 제 걱정이 늘 근심거리였어요.
examples.en: For my parents, worrying about me was always a concern.

examples.ko: 근심거리를 혼자 안고 있지 말고 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't carry your worries alone, tell someone.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나니 근심거리 하나가 사라졌어요.
examples.en: Now that the exam is over, one worry is gone.

examples.ko: 건강 문제가 요즘 새 근심거리로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A health problem has become a new worry lately.

explain: '걱정거리'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. '근심'은 조금 글이나 점잖은 말투에 어울리고, 일상 대화에서는 '걱정거리'를 더 자연스럽게 느끼는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: If you have something to worry about, please tell me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning but more natural in everyday talk.

phrases.en: A new worry has come up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정할 일이 새로 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a new thing to worry about appears.

phrases.en: I was relieved of my worries after hearing I passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이 줄어들거나 없어졌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when worries lessen or go away.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as '걱정거리'. '근심' sounds a bit more written or formal, and many people find '걱정거리' more natural in everyday talk.

en: to be shocked; to be startled; to be astonished

examples.ko: 바퀴벌레를 보고 동생이 기겁했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling freaked out when he saw a cockroach.

examples.ko: 수도 요금이 너무 많이 나와서 기겁해서 전화했어요.
examples.en: The water bill was so high that I was shocked and called them.

examples.ko: 기겁할 정도로 방이 지저분했어요.
examples.en: The room was so messy it was shocking.

examples.ko: 아이가 기겁하며 엄마 품으로 뛰어갔어요.
examples.en: The child ran into his mother's arms in a fright.

examples.ko: 길에서 큰 개를 만나면 저는 항상 기겁해요.
examples.en: I always get terrified when I meet a big dog on the street.

examples.ko: 친구들이 기겁하지 않게 천천히 얘기해 주세요.
examples.en: Please speak slowly so that my friends don't get a shock.

explain: '놀라다'보다 훨씬 크게, 몸이 움찔할 만큼 놀랄 때 써요. 무서운 것, 징그러운 것, 예상 못 한 큰 금액 같은 데에 자주 써요. '기겁을 하다'라고 말하기도 하고, 편한 대화에서 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I was horrified when I saw a mouse.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기겁하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 '을'이 들어가 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 기겁하다, but with 을 it sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: I was terrified at the sight of a snake and ran away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀란 뒤에 바로 이어지는 행동을 '-아/어서'로 연결해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -아/어서 form links the shock with what you did right after.

phrases.en: The door suddenly opened, and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기겁하다'보다 약하고 더 일상적으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Milder and more everyday than 기겁하다.

explain_en: It describes being startled much more strongly than '놀라다', enough to make your body jump. It is often used for scary or gross things, or an unexpectedly large amount of money. People also say '기겁을 하다', and it fits casual conversation well.
